verdict.rationale: Fedora is an installable OS, so this axis applies. The docs never directly address hardware choice or vendor lock-in; the closest point is that apps can be installed from Fedora's repositories, Flathub 'or anywhere else' (fedora-docs-8). Community reports describe it working well out of the box, including restored suspend on Nvidia (fedora-comm-5, fedora-comm-6). They also report caveats: Nvidia driver pain, Wayland trouble on older hardware, a broken display inside VirtualBox, and no CUDA support (fedora-comm-6, fedora-comm-19, fedora-comm-10, fedora-comm-9). Missing for 10: first-party documentation of supported hardware and architectures, any explicit statement on freedom from vendor lock-in, and reliable proprietary GPU driver support.
